US urges Ethiopia, Eritrea to show restraint The United States urged Ethiopia and Eritrea to exercise maximum restraint amid rising cross-border tensions, warning that a new military conflict could trigger a severe humanitarian crisis across the Horn of Africa and jeopardise ongoing bilateral cooperation. ANI | Updated: 04-10-2026 10:59 IST | Created: 04-10-2026 10:59 IST

The seal of the United States Department of State is seen in Washington, US. (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Amid escalating cross-border frictions between Ethiopia and Eritrea, the United States urged both nations Saturday to exercise “maximum restraint”, cautioning that any fresh hostilities risk precipitating an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe across the Horn of Africa. In an official release, the State Department stressed that the worsening discord carries wide-ranging regional ramifications. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott remarked, “Increasing cross-border tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea have the potential to affect the entire region.” Emphasising the fragility of the area, Pigott added, “The Horn of Africa cannot sustain another military conflict and humanitarian crisis. A conflict jeopardises ongoing US collaboration on shared interests with both countries.” Washington further appealed to Addis Ababa and Asmara to uphold international norms concerning territorial sovereignty while abandoning any escalatory measures. Stressing the necessity for diplomatic channels, Pigott stated, “We strongly urge Ethiopia and Eritrea to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of their neighbors, exercise maximum restraint and return to dialogue and cooperation as agreed in their 2018 peace framework.” He concluded by noting that “Peace through dialogue is the only path toward sustainable security, economic growth, and prosperity.” This diplomatic intervention arrives as security conditions within northern Ethiopia deteriorate alongside sliding bilateral relations. Rather than introducing punitive actions or sanctions, the recent US advisory prioritised de-escalation, pointing back to the 2018 accord that resolved their historical hostilities. Tensions have mounted following renewed hostilities in Ethiopia's northern Tigray zone. Consequently, official US travel advisories currently instruct citizens to avoid travel to the Tigray region and the Eritrean border due to ongoing armed conflict and volatility. Diplomatic relations between the two neighbours have experienced severe instability over the past three decades. Following a prolonged struggle for independence, Eritrea formally separated from Ethiopia in 1993, which later culminated in a destructive border war spanning from 1998 to 2000 that claimed tens of thousands of lives. Ties remained strained until a historic rapprochement in 2018, when Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki successfully restored bilateral relations. (ANI)

item.description: The administration made no public announcements regarding the gathering, which transpired as negotiations with Tehran remained deadlocked.

Trump team discusses Iran war, Yemen situation in Camp David huddle: Report  The administration made no public announcements regarding the gathering, which transpired as negotiations with Tehran remained deadlocked. ANI | Updated: 04-10-2026 10:53 IST | Created: 04-10-2026 10:53 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump’s top national security aides held an unpublicised meeting at Camp David on Friday, conferring for several hours to discuss next steps in the war with Iran alongside the Saudi-backed campaign targeting Houthi rebels in Yemen, Axios reported, citing three US officials. The administration made no public announcements regarding the gathering, which transpired as negotiations with Tehran remained deadlocked. Trump Administration is weighing whether to re-engage in major combat operations against the Iran. Vice President JD Vance presided over the discussions. He was joined by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, US War Secretary Peter Hegseth, White House envoy Steve Witkoff, CIA Director John Ratcliffe, and Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Gen Dan Caine and other senior officials. Commenting on the deliberations regarding the Middle East crisis, a US official noted that critical matters were determined or evaluated. The White House declined to issue a statement concerning the gathering. The high-level session unfolded as President Trump approaches a decisive juncture regarding the trajectory of the American campaign against Iran. “Now I have to make a decision: either Iran signs the deal, or it won’t exist any longer,” President Donald Trump had said on Thursday. When pressed by reporters on Friday afternoon regarding his prospective strategy while his advisers were holding discussions at Camp David, President Trump remarked, “If I told you, you would have a major story,” before adding, “But you will see. It is working out very well. Iran is not doing well.” Beyond the Iranian dossier, the Camp David talks also addressed the escalating Saudi-backed push against Houthi forces in Yemen. Riyadh is reportedly preparing a prospective offensive against the Houthis, actively lobbying Washington to provide air support through US airstrikes. Although President Trump has hitherto shown reluctance to participate in the operation, American officials indicated that his stance remains subject to change. Such high-level strategy sessions at Camp David remain a rarity, with the most recent comparable meeting occurring in June 2025 shortly before the outbreak of war between Israel and Iran. (ANI)

item.title: ‘Have no intention of stopping’: Bryan Cranston, 70, on continuing to work
item.description: Speaking to PEOPLE while attending ArtPrize, an annual art competition and cultural festival in Grand Rapids, Michigan, Cranston said he wants to continue working for as long as he can.
item.content:encoded:
‘Have no intention of stopping’: Bryan Cranston, 70, on continuing to work Speaking to PEOPLE while attending ArtPrize, an annual art competition and cultural festival in Grand Rapids, Michigan, Cranston said he wants to continue working for as long as he can. ANI | Updated: 04-10-2026 08:50 IST | Created: 04-10-2026 08:50 IST

Bryan Cranston (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Actor Bryan Cranston has no plans to slow down his work anytime soon. The 70-year-old actor, known for shows such as Breaking Bad and Malcolm in the Middle, said he cannot imagine retiring from acting and writing. Speaking to PEOPLE while attending ArtPrize, an annual art competition and cultural festival in Grand Rapids, Michigan, Cranston said he wants to continue working for as long as he can. “For an actor living the life that I am very fortunate to have, I have no intention of stopping, and I think life will stop before I will want it to, and that will be great,” Cranston said. The actor added that retirement is not something he sees himself choosing, saying that acting and writing are a major part of his life. “It’s like stopping breathing for me. If I stopped acting and writing, what would I do? I’m not one that’s going to sit on the porch, just because I’m of that age,” continues the actor. “Some people cannot wait for retirement, but I wouldn’t know what to do with it.” Cranston also spoke about how he wants to look back on his life when the time comes. He said he hopes to have lived and worked enough to feel that he has nothing left to give. “Someone once said, ‘When all is said and done, and it’s time for me to leave the earth, I want to be completely worn out,’ and I think that’s a good way to [go],” adds Cranston. “I want to be absolutely completely worn out, like, I got nothing left.” “I did everything, I traveled, I experienced life, and I’m tired and I’m just absolutely done,” he further explains. “I want to be able to be proud of the things that I’ve [accomplished].” Cranston comes from a family with a long connection to acting. His parents, Joseph Louis Cranston and Annalisa “Peggy” Cranston, were actors, and he is part of a family that has four generations of actors. His daughter, Taylor Dearden, has also earned praise for her role as Dr. Melissa “Mel” King in The Pitt. The actor has played several well-known characters during his career, including Walter White in Breaking Bad and Hal in Malcolm in the Middle. He has also appeared in films such as Trumbo and Argo and worked in theatre in productions including All the Way, Network and All My Sons. Cranston has also worked as a writer, producer and director. His career has earned him several Emmy and Tony Awards, along with a Laurence Olivier Award and a Golden Globe Award. He has also received nominations for an Academy Award and a British Academy Film Award. Looking back at how his interest in acting began, Cranston recalled growing up around his actor parents. He said watching them work eventually led him to try performing himself. “[My siblings and I], we were watching our parents do things like, my dad’s doing a movie here, my mom’s doing a commercial there, and the first play I ever did was in our garage. My brother wrote and directed it, so he was my very first director,” the actor says. “I think we charged the neighbor kids a nickel to come see it, and that included a glass of punch or something,” he continues with a laugh. “So once you get that sense of performing, even if it’s a garage production of something, once you do that, it either ignites something, or you never want to do that again,” Cranston adds. “Or sometimes it’s like, ‘Well, that was fun. I’m glad I did it, but I don’t need to do it anymore.’" (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Yemeni forces confirm strikes on Houthi-controlled Sanaa, Saada after rebel group targets Aramco facility in Riyadh Yemen's internationally recognised government on Saturday (local time) confirmed strikes against what it described as "vital targets" of the Houthis in Sanaa and Saada, after the rebel group claimed it carried out a missile and drone operation targeting Aramco facilities in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh. ANI | Updated: 04-10-2026 08:00 IST | Created: 04-10-2026 08:00 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Yemen

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Yemen's internationally recognised government on Saturday (local time) confirmed strikes against what it described as "vital targets" of the Houthis in Sanaa and Saada, after the rebel group claimed it carried out a missile and drone operation targeting Aramco facilities in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh. The developments mark a fresh escalation in the ongoing conflict, with both sides issuing statements claiming military actions. In a statement issued by the media centre of the Armed Forces of Yemen's internationally recognised government, the official spokesperson said Yemeni forces were carrying out strikes against Houthi-controlled areas. "We are delivering painful strikes against vital targets of the terrorist Houthi militia in Sanaa and Saada," the official spokesperson said. The spokesperson further warned that Houthi military capabilities would remain under attack. "The capabilities of the Houthi militia will not be safe from the fire of our armed forces, and we will destroy them," the spokesperson added. The statement came after the Houthi group said it had launched a military operation targeting Aramco in Riyadh using ballistic missiles and drones. According to a statement issued by Houthi military spokesperson Brigadier General Yahya Saree, the attack was carried out in response to what the group described as Saudi strikes against Sanaa and other areas under its control. "In response to the Saudi aggression against the capital, Sana'a, and the liberated provinces, which in the past 24 hours reached up to 60 airstrikes and missile attacks, bringing the total number of Saudi aggression attacks since the escalation against our country to 1,410," the Houthi statement said. The Houthi group said that it carried out a "qualitative military operation" using ballistic missiles and drones against Aramco facilities in Riyadh. The group claimed that the operation achieved its objective and said fires broke out at the targeted sites. "The operation successfully achieved its objective, thanks to Allah," the statement said. "The strikes were precise and direct, resulting in fire breaking out at the targeted sites," it added. The Houthi statement also warned of further escalation, saying the group would respond to what it described as attacks against Yemen and its people. "The shedding of Yemeni blood with such criminality and brutality necessitates that the armed forces, along with all the free people of our nation, take all necessary escalatory steps and deterrent measures to affirm to everyone that the price for disregarding the blood of our faithful people will be high and exorbitant, and the criminal enemy must understand that continuing to shed our people's blood will cost them dearly," the statement said. The group further said it would continue its policy of escalation until the attacks and blockade against Yemen end. "We will continue to impose the equation of "a siege for a siege", and "an escalation for escalation", and targeting the Saudi enemy's troop buildups until the aggression ceases and the siege on our beloved country is lifted," the statement said. The latest exchange of strikes comes amid continuing tensions involving Yemen's internationally recognised government, the Houthi group and Saudi Arabia, with both sides accusing the other of escalating military action. (ANI)
